Subject: Invoice routing & entity mapping — Medisure onboarding

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we start the technical setup for monthly invoicing, we need the invoices to be split across two legal entities in our group (MediSure US and MediSure EU). Requirements summary below:

- Invoice lines for US customers should bill to MediSure US (EIN: 12-3456789).
- EU customers (non-US billing addresses) should bill to MediSure EU (VAT: EU123456789).
- Maintain a single consolidated PDF per invoice number for our records, but send account statements separately to each entity's AP contact.

Can you share your recommended mapping template and any routing rules Redwood needs to support this? Also: do you support per-line tax tagging so we can run VAT reclaim?

Attaching our current entity reference export (medisure_entity_mapping.xlsx) — it includes customer IDs and country tags.

Next steps: if you can send a short checklist of config items we should prepare (legal IDs, remit addresses, preferred invoice XML schema), we can get procurement signed off and schedule the integration.

Best,
Liam
Head of Revenue Operations
MediSure Health

Subject: Re: Invoice routing & entity mapping — Medisure onboarding

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Happy to run this through with Marcus on finance rules. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, Redwood supports per-line entity assignments and tax tags; our routing engine can emit invoice PDFs that include split ledger rows and also export per-entity statements.
- We can keep a single invoice number and generate per-entity remittance views.

Requested from your side (checklist):
1) Confirm legal identifiers for each entity (EIN / VAT).
2) Provide preferred remit addresses and AP contact emails for both entities.
3) Indicate whether you want tax applied at line-level (recommended) or as an entity-level adjustment.
4) If you use a specific XML/Peppol schema for automated ingestion, send a sample.

I've attached a lightweight template we use to map customers to entities (initial_entity_map_template.csv). Ben — can you take point on the onboarding timeline once Liam confirms the checklist items? Marcus, can you confirm any Redwood-side accounting constraints we should flag to procurement?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medisure.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:20:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice routing & entity mapping — Medisure onboarding

Tessa / Liam — looped in to add the finance perspective. A few practical notes and suggested routing rules:

- We will map each customer record to a single primary legal entity (customer->entity). For split accounts (same customer buys under multiple countries), we'll support per-invoice-line overrides using the country field you already have in the spreadsheet.
- Tax handling: we recommend tagging VAT at the line level and storing VAT amounts per entity. That makes reclaim and reporting simpler.
- Consolidated PDF: Redwood can produce a consolidated PDF where we render section headers for each entity and include a summary ledger page that shows per-entity totals and tax lines. The PDF metadata will include entity tags for downstream ingestion.

Routing rules (draft):
1) If billing_address.country == "US" -> Entity = MediSure US (EIN 12-3456789).
2) Else if billing_address.country in EU_member_list -> Entity = MediSure EU (VAT EU123456789).
3) Else fallback -> Entity = MediSure US (treat non-EU as US for your reporting).
4) For manual overrides, Redwood will accept a customer_metadata.entity_id field from your CRM export.

Action items for Medisure:
- Provide official remit addresses and AP contact emails (we'll place in the account config).
- Confirm whether your accounting team prefers separate GL codes per entity or a single GL with entity dimension — this affects the CSV export format.

Attaching a short doc with the routing rules and examples (routing_rules_draft.md). Happy to schedule a 30-min call to walk through examples.

— Marcus
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
